advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin a version constraint (e.g. lower bound) on `genai-prices` in the `pricing` extra, consistent with every other extra.
evidence: pyproject.toml:134-136: `pricing = [\n    "genai-prices",\n]`
pyproject.toml:128 `"inspect-ai>=0.3.221",` and pyproject.toml:152-153 `"tree-sitter>=0.21"` / `"tree-sitter-language-pack>=0.2"` and pyproject.toml:161 `"pyright>=1.1"` all pin a lower bound
usage_log.py:194-200 calls `pricing.calc_price(pricing.Usage(**usage_kwargs(row)), model_ref=..., provider_id=..., genai_request_timestamp=...)` and `price.total_price` — a fixed API contract
advisory.finding: The new `genai-prices` optional dependency is declared with no version constraint, unlike every other extra in pyproject.toml (e.g. `inspect-ai>=0.3.221`, `tree-sitter>=0.21`, `lizard>=1.23`, `pyright>=1.1`). The pricing code depends on a precise API surface (`calc_price(usage, model_ref=, provider_id=, genai_request_timestamp=)`, `Usage(**four_token_fields)`, `price.total_price`, typed `LookupError`); an unpinned dep can pull a future release that changes that surface and silently degrade all pricing.
scenarios: A future genai-prices major release renames a kwarg or the Usage field names; a fresh `pip install 'nava-rebar[pricing]'` resolves it and the pricing path breaks.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `"genai-prices"` with a bounded spec such as `"genai-prices>=X.Y"` matching the API the code targets.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add at least one test (guarded by importorskip on genai-prices) that prices a known model against the real installed library to validate the calc_price/Usage/total_price contract.
evidence: tests/unit/test_usage_log.py:145-155: `stub = types.ModuleType("genai_prices") ... stub.Usage = Usage ... stub.calc_price = calc_price ... monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "genai_prices", stub)`
usage_log.py:203-205: `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 ... logger.warning(...); return None` swallows any real API mismatch into 'unpriced'
ABSENCE: no test invokes the real installed genai-prices `calc_price`/`Usage` to confirm the kwargs and `total_price` attribute names the adapter relies on
advisory.finding: The pricing unit tests stub the entire `genai_prices` module (fake `Usage`/`calc_price`), so the real library's API contract — the `calc_price` kwarg names (`model_ref`, `provider_id`, `genai_request_timestamp`), `Usage(**four token fields)`, and `price.total_price` — is never exercised against the installed package. Because `_price_row` swallows any non-LookupError into a WARNING + 'unpriced', a real-library signature mismatch would fail open (every row unpriced) with no test detecting it.
scenarios: The real genai-prices API differs from (or drifts from) the stub's assumed signature; pricing silently yields 0 priced rows and a per-row WARNING flood, while all tests still pass.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin `genai-prices` with at least a lower-bound version constraint (e.g. `genai-prices>=X.Y`) consistent with the `eval` extra.
evidence: "pricing = [\n    \"genai-prices\",\n]"
Sibling extra pins: `eval = [ "inspect-ai>=0.3.221" ]`
Diff adds `pricing = [ "genai-prices" ]` to pyproject.toml but the changed-files list contains no lockfile.
ABSENCE: no uv.lock/poetry.lock hunk present in the 5 changed files.
advisory.finding: The new optional dependency `genai-prices` is added with no version constraint, unlike the sibling `eval` extra which pins `inspect-ai>=0.3.221`. An unpinned dep resolves to whatever the latest version is at install time, exposing the build to upstream breaking changes or a compromised release.
merged_from: No lockfile (e.g. uv.lock / poetry.lock / requirements) update accompanies the new `pricing` extra in the diff; if the project uses a committed lockfile the optional dependency may be missing from it, leaving the manifest and lock out of sync.
scenarios: A new genai-prices release changes the `calc_price`/`Usage` API or `total_price` attribute, causing every priced row to hit the broad `except Exception` WARNING path and silently report all calls unpriced.
A malicious or yanked upstream release is picked up because no floor/ceiling constrains resolution.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a version floor pinning the genai-prices release whose API (`Usage`, `calc_price`, `total_price`) this code was written against.
evidence:
"price = pricing.calc_price(
            pricing.Usage(**usage_kwargs(row)),
            model_ref=str(model),
            provider_id=row.get("provider") or None,
            genai_request_timestamp=timestamp,
        )"
No version constraint in pyproject.toml pins the API surface these calls rely on.
advisory.finding: The code depends on specific genai-prices API symbols (`Usage`, `calc_price`, kwargs `model_ref`/`provider_id`/`genai_request_timestamp`, and `price.total_price`) but with the dependency unpinned there is no version floor guaranteeing those symbols exist; any API drift is only caught by the broad `except Exception` in `_price_row`, silently marking all calls unpriced.
scenarios: Upstream renames `calc_price` or the `total_price` field in a future release; the guard swallows the AttributeError as a WARNING and every row becomes unpriced with no hard failure surfaced to CI.

evidence: src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:252-255 accumulates `per_model.setdefault(model, ...)` keyed by each row's own model

test_summarize_prices_known_rows writes two rows both with model 'claude-opus-4-8' (tests/unit/test_usage_log.py:206,217) — no test uses two DISTINCT models

ABSENCE: no test asserts multiple '| <model> | <calls> | $<cost> |' rollup rows or per-model cost separation, despite the diff/docs claiming 'per-model rollup table' and 'multi-model ops sum correctly row by row'
advisory.finding: The new per-model rollup and the 'multi-model ops sum row by row' behavior are only tested with a single model, so a regression that mis-keys or collapses per-model aggregation (e.g. attributing all cost to one model, or emitting only one rollup row) would not be caught.
scenarios: A summarize run over a log containing calls to two or more distinct models
A refactor that accidentally keys the rollup on op instead of model, or overwrites rather than accumulates per model
